name: Medeu / Almaly District
tagline: Central grid, cafes and walkable blocks
description: The leafy central grid around Panfilov Park and Arbat pedestrian street. Tree-lined avenues, Soviet-era apartments, coffee shops and coworking spaces sit within easy walking distance of restaurants, museums and the Green Bazaar.
bestFor: First-time visitors and nomads wanting cafes, coworking and everything within walking distance

name: Bostandyk District
description: A newer district in the south of the city climbing toward the Tien Shan foothills. It mixes modern residential towers with malls, universities and mountain views, offering quieter streets and cleaner air than the dense center.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting newer apartments, mountain views and a calmer pace

name: Samal Microdistrict
description: A prestigious residential pocket south of the center, known for landscaped courtyards, embassies and higher-end apartments. It sits close to the Palace of the Republic and Kok Tobe cable car, blending quiet streets with quick access downtown.
bestFor: Remote workers with budget wanting a calm, safe, central-adjacent base

name: Auezov District
description: A large residential district west of the center built mostly of Soviet microdistricts. It is affordable, fully local and served by the metro, with plenty of markets, bakeries and everyday shops rather than tourist polish.
bestFor: Budget nomads and longer stays wanting cheaper rent and authentic daily life
